transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-25 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Jesse Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (NorthStar CTO), Maya Lopez (Head of MLOps), Alex Ruiz (SRE)

Summary: Discovery focused on per-unit economics and deployment model tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer is budget conscious, wants predictable unit costs for a recommendation system and conversational assistants; interested in batching, KV/prefix cache, and reserved capacity options.

00:00 Jesse: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm Jesse, AE at Redwood, and Priya our systems engineer. today's goal is to understand your workloads and constraints around cost per inference and capacity.
00:18 Daniel: Thanks, yeah we want to zero in on per-token cost — we have a POC budget and then a narrower forecast for production. we run a recommender that makes ~1.2M calls/day and a conversation assistant for support handles bursts.
00:30 Maya: avg prompt length for recs is around 120 tokens, completion ~80 tokens, but for convo it's variable, 40-600 tokens depending on session.
00:44 Priya: ok that helps. are you leaning hosted or self-managed? any regulatory reqs?
00:50 Daniel: initial goal is hosted to move fast but if costs explode or we need VPC/keys, we'll consider dedicated or private. we also need SOC2 and SSO.
01:05 Jesse: totally. on hosted we typically price per-token plus embedding units; for dedicated you get reserved capacity pricing — much lower per-token effective cost depending on utilization and batch settings.
01:20 Alex: can you walk through the batching and cache levers? we care about tail latency but also unit economics.
01:30 Priya: sure — two levers. batching increases throughput by aggregating requests so the GPU amortizes work, lowering tokens per second cost. cache/prefix KV caching avoids regenerating earlier tokens for repeated prefixes — huge for chat or templated prompts. combined, customers often see 20-60% reduction in per-token spend depending on hit rate and request distribution.
01:56 Maya: what's realistic for us? our reco calls are highly repetitive, same templates, so high cache hit rate. convo less so.
02:07 Priya: for recs you could see up to 60% reduction if you get prefix cache hit rates of 40-70%. for convo maybe 10-25% unless you implement session-level caching.
02:22 Daniel: and batch sizes? how does that affect latency? our SLO for support is p95 < 400ms.
02:30 Priya: batching trades off single-request latency for throughput. continuous batching in our runtime keeps batching windows tight; for small requests (150 tokens) you can maintain p95 ~150-250ms with batching enabled. if you need strict <100ms, dedicated GPUs with optimized kernel selection and lower batch windows may be needed.
02:53 Jesse: important to map your traffic curve — average qps, burst qps, token distribution. pricing on dedicated is typically a capacity seat + lower effective per-token when fully utilized. hosted is simpler but needs more attention to batching/caching to control cost.
03:10 Alex: any numbers to ballpark? we need something to compare against in our budget model.
03:16 Jesse: rough example — for hosted, if you assume 200 token roundtrip per call and 1M calls month, that's 200M tokens. if hosted is roughly $0.00045 per 1k tokens for generation (hypothetical for discussion), that would be about $90k/mo before batching/cache improvements. with caching and batching you might reduce to $40-70k. dedicated reserved might be a fixed monthly for GPUs + much lower marginal.
03:46 Maya: ok that's useful — we don't need exact numbers now but we need an apples-to-apples pricing sheet.
03:53 Priya: we'll send a hosted vs dedicated comparison using your traffic profile. also we'll run feasibility on quantization — moving from fp16 to int8 or q4 variants can lower cost per token on dedicated GPU and sometimes on hosted via quantized model variants.
04:09 Daniel: do you support customer-managed keys? we can't send PII to third party without keys.
04:15 Jesse: yes, for Dedicated and Private we support KMS/HSM integrations. hosted has options for encrypted-at-rest and audit logs, and we can discuss bring-your-own-key in enterprise plan.
04:26 Alex: network egress — our infra approval is strict. private deployment is possible on-prem but that requires more runbook time. what's the rollout timeline for private?
04:36 Priya: private can be weeks to a few months depending on environment, networking, and security review. Dedicated is quicker — we can provision reserved capacity in days to weeks.
04:46 Maya: what about quality regressions with quantized models? we care about precision for recommendations.
04:50 Priya: we run evals and can recommend quantization profile per model and workload; often q4_0 or q8_0 profiles have minimal impact on quality for retrieval/recommendation tasks but we validate with your eval set.
05:05 Daniel: ok cool. on utilization — what's the tipping point where dedicated makes sense? our CFO wants a break-even calc.
05:12 Jesse: typical rule — if you have consistent sustained utilization close to a few hundred TFLOPs-hours or predictable gamma of calls where monthly token-equivalent costs exceed the reserved monthly commitment, dedicated wins. practically many customers cross over when their monthly hosted spend is in the tens of thousands and predictable. we'll produce a model comparing cost vs utilization given your numbers.
05:33 Maya: we have some seasonality — end-of-month spikes 3x baseline. can Redwood autoscale for dedicated?
05:40 Priya: yes, dedicated pools can autoscale and burst to the hosted pool or other variants to handle spikes. routing policy can fall back to lower-cost or higher-latency variants depending on policy.
05:54 Alex: any compliance references? we need SOC2, ISO, audit logs, RBAC, SSO, certs.
06:00 Jesse: we'll attach SOC2 and ISO docs and include audit log details; we have RBAC and SSO via SAML/OIDC.
06:10 Daniel: ok next steps — send pricing, security docs, and schedule bench.
06:15 Jesse: noted. Priya will follow up for technical deep dive.

Crosstalk and clarifying Qs 06:20-15:00 (transcript excerpts)
06:20 Maya: one more question — embeddings pricing for vector search, we run nightly indexing of 2M items, do you price per-embedding?
06:28 Priya: yes embeddings are per-unit as well; we can suggest batch embedding flows to reduce unit cost. nightly offline jobs can always be done on Dedicated or customer-managed infra to save hosted costs.
06:40 Daniel: curious about benchmark options — can Redwood run a benchmark using our sample prompts?
06:45 Priya: yes, we can run a POC benchmark in hosted or dedicated trial; we'll need sample prompts and a traffic profile. we can also run a microbenchmark on a quantized variant to measure latency/cost.
07:02 Alex: and logging retention — how long do you keep transcripts?
07:07 Jesse: default retention is 30 days for hosted logs; enterprise tiers can extend retention or allow export to your storage. Private keeps logs in your control.
07:14 Maya: ok great. can you explain how cache invalidation works? we have updating item catalogs — stale cache is a concern.
07:22 Priya: cache invalidation can be time-based or event-driven; for catalog updates you can push invalidation events or use short TTLs for affected prefixes. PV-based solutions exist for completely dynamic content.
07:40 Daniel: will you give us an example of per-request cost with batching?
07:44 Priya: example — single small request 100 tokens might cost X, but if batched with 16 requests average effective cost per request drops by ~50-70% depending on model and hardware. we'll surface numbers in the pricing sheet using your distribution.
08:00 Jesse: any immediate blockers on your side for a POC?
08:05 Maya: budget sign-off and security review; we need SOC2 and network diagrams.
08:10 Daniel: timeline — pilot in 4 weeks if we can get a clear cost model and bench results.
08:15 Jesse: sounds good. we'll target to get the pricing + security docs to you in 48 hours and schedule the deep-dive for next week.

Wrap-up 08:16-48m mark
08:16 Jesse: recap: Jesse to send pricing + hosted vs dedicated comparison; Priya to schedule technical deep-dive and run bench on sample prompts; Maya to provide traffic profile and logs; Alex to confirm networking constraints.
08:30 Daniel: thanks everyone. excited to see the numbers.
08:33 Priya: i'll put calendar invites after the call.
08:36 Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription quality: Some proper nouns and acronyms may be mis-recognized (e.g., KV cache spelled out, KMS/HSM sometimes heard as KMSH). occasional speaker overlap and filler words retained.
